prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

In one aspect, there is provided a method comprising: receiving consumption data comprising readings from one or more utility meters associated with a property comprising one or more devices, the one or more devices comprising one or more devices of interest; determining, in the received consumption data, one or more positive consumption variations indicative of switching on of one or more of the devices and/or one or more negative consumption variations indicative of switching off of one or more of the devices; identifying one or more events associated with the one or more devices, based on the determined variations, by matching one or more positive variations with one or more negative variations; grouping the identified one or more events into one or more blocks, each block corresponding to an occurrence of usage of a device of the property; classifying the one or more blocks into one or more predetermined clusters, the one or more predetermined clusters comprising a respective predetermined cluster associated with each device of interest of the property; and determining an occurrence and/or an absence of usage of the one or more devices of interest of the property, based on the classification into the one or more predetermined clusters.

outputs.L1: In one aspect, there is provided a method comprising: receiving consumption data comprising readings from one or more utility meters associated with a property comprising one or more devices, the one or more devices comprising one or more devices of interest; determining, within the received consumption data, one or more positive consumption variations indicative of one or more of the devices being switched on and/or one or more negative consumption variations indicative of one or more of the devices being switched off; identifying one or more events associated with the one or more devices, based on the determined variations, by matching one or more positive variations with one or more negative variations; grouping the identified one or more events into one or more blocks, each block corresponding to an occurrence of usage of a device of the property; classifying the one or more blocks into one or more predetermined clusters, the one or more predetermined clusters comprising a respective predetermined cluster associated with each device of interest of the property; and determining an occurrence and/or an absence of usage of the one or more devices of interest of the property based on the classification into the one or more predetermined clusters.
outputs.L2: In one implementation, a method is provided that includes obtaining consumption information containing measurements from one or more utility meters linked to a property that includes one or more devices, among which are one or more devices of interest. Within the obtained consumption information, the method detects one or more increases in consumption that suggest one or more devices have been turned on and/or one or more decreases in consumption that suggest one or more devices have been turned off. Using the detected changes, the method identifies one or more device-related events by associating one or more consumption increases with one or more consumption decreases. The identified events are then arranged into one or more groups, with each group representing an instance in which a device at the property was used. The method further assigns the one or more groups to one or more predefined clusters, where the predefined clusters include a corresponding cluster for each device of interest at the property. Based on this assignment to the predefined clusters, the method determines whether usage of the one or more devices of interest at the property occurred and/or was absent.
outputs.L3:
The method receives consumption data from one or more utility meters associated with a property that includes multiple devices. The consumption data may represent, for example, electricity, gas, water, or another utility consumed within the property. Because several devices may contribute to the total measured consumption, the received data reflects the combined activity of those devices over time.

The method analyzes the consumption data to detect variations in consumption. In particular, it identifies positive consumption variations, which may indicate that a device has been switched on or has started operating, and negative consumption variations, which may indicate that a device has been switched off or has stopped operating. These variations are detected by monitoring changes in the measured consumption level and determining whether such changes correspond to meaningful increases or decreases.

After detecting the positive and negative consumption variations, the method identifies device-related events by matching positive variations with corresponding negative variations. A matched pair may represent a complete operating cycle or usage interval of a device, beginning when the device is switched on and ending when the device is switched off. By associating increases in consumption with subsequent decreases of a similar magnitude or pattern, the method can distinguish individual device events from the aggregate consumption signal.

The identified events are then grouped into blocks. Each block represents an occurrence of device usage and may include one or more related events that occur within a defined time period or share similar consumption characteristics. Grouping the events into blocks allows the method to describe a device usage occurrence in a structured manner, such as by its start time, end time, duration, consumption level, total energy usage, or other relevant features.

The method then classifies the blocks into predetermined clusters. These clusters may correspond to known or expected patterns of device usage. By assigning each block to one of the predetermined clusters, the method determines whether one or more devices of interest were used or not used during the relevant period. In this way, the method can infer device activity from aggregated utility meter data without requiring separate monitoring of each individual device.
outputs.L4:
The method provides a way to determine whether particular devices or appliances at a property have been used by analyzing aggregate utility meter consumption data, such as electricity, gas, or water usage readings. Instead of requiring a separate sensor on each device, the method examines changes in the overall consumption recorded by a utility meter and identifies patterns that correspond to the operation of individual devices.

The process begins by obtaining a time series of utility meter readings for a property. These readings may represent total consumption over time or interval-based usage values. The data is analyzed to detect variations in consumption, including positive variations, which may indicate that a device has turned on or increased its usage, and negative variations, which may indicate that a device has turned off or reduced its usage. Each detected variation may be characterized by attributes such as magnitude, time of occurrence, duration, and rate of change.

The method then attempts to match positive and negative variations that appear to be related. For example, a positive increase in consumption may be paired with a later negative decrease of similar size, suggesting that a device began operating at the time of the positive variation and stopped operating at the time of the negative variation. These matched pairs are treated as device events. A device event may represent a single cycle of operation, such as a heater turning on and off, a pump running for a period of time, or an appliance drawing power during a usage cycle.

After identifying individual device events, the method groups related events into usage blocks. A usage block may include one event or multiple events that occur close together in time or that exhibit a recurring pattern associated with a single device or device category. For instance, repeated on/off cycles occurring during a defined period may be grouped as one usage block corresponding to the operation of a thermostat-controlled appliance, irrigation system, pool pump, water heater, or other device of interest.

Each usage block is then compared with predefined device-specific clusters. These clusters represent known or expected usage characteristics for particular devices. A cluster may be defined using features such as consumption level, event duration, frequency, time of day, total usage, number of cycles, or other statistical or behavioral attributes. By comparing the characteristics of a detected usage block with these predefined clusters, the method classifies the block as likely corresponding to a particular device or device type.

Based on this classification, the method determines whether one or more devices of interest were used at the property during the analyzed time period. The output may indicate device usage, non-usage, frequency of use, timing of use, estimated duration, or estimated consumption attributable to the device. This information can be used for monitoring, reporting, diagnostics, customer engagement, energy or water efficiency analysis, maintenance detection, or verification of device operation.

In this way, the method supports device-level usage detection from aggregate utility meter data. It allows meaningful information about individual device behavior to be inferred without requiring direct device instrumentation, thereby enabling more detailed insights into property-level consumption patterns using existing meter readings.
